atoms.text: Now Milo is going to show you around some boreal forests.

instruction.text: Select the photo of a boreal forest.

hint.label: Boreal
hint.text: Boreal is another way of saying northern.

feedback.end: Correct! Boreal forests are forests found in cold climates in the north of the planet, for example in Canada or Norway. We don’t get boreal forests in the UK.

instruction.text: This is a forest in Alaska in the USA. Select the trees to learn more about boreal forests.

text: Boreal forests have lots of coniferous trees. Coniferous trees are trees with needles instead of leaves. Needles are better at conserving water, which helps the trees survive harsh winters.

atoms.a: “What kind of animal can you see?”
atoms.sound: ssml: <voice voiceLang='en' voice='m7'>What kind of animal can you see</voice>

text: Animals in boreal forests normally have lots of fur so they can survive the cold winters. Another example, is a wolf - look at how thick its fur is!

instruction.text: Here is another boreal forest in Canada. Select the fire to learn more.

feedback.end: Wildfires are a natural feature of boreal forests. They can be destructive, but they also clear the way for new growth.

atoms.a: We find boreal forests in the UK.

feedback.wrong: The UK only has temperate forests.

atoms.a: Animals in boreal forests normally have thick fur.
Wildfires are a natural process in boreal forests.
